title: Post-hoc derivation of a quality-coupled Q30 acceptance threshold
question: On the immutable D12.12-H1 Blender 5.2 arrays, does a globally quality-coupled risk threshold at or below 32768 Q30 remove every accepted quality violation while retaining the unchanged 0.97 cell and 0.95 per-owner coverage gates?
decisionRole: Derive or reject a threshold candidate for a separately preregistered future holdout. This experiment cannot repair or reverse the rejected D12.12-H1 verdict.

requirements: This spec, all four new tool paths and the output root are absent when preregistration begins.
This exact spec is committed and pushed before any new tool byte exists.
All four tools are committed before the output root exists.
No Blender render, model call or network call occurs.
Only immutable D12.12-H1 adapter and consumer arrays are measurement inputs.
D12.12-H1 formal Git tree remains exact before and after this derivation.
No threshold, gate, denominator, selection order or verdict mapping changes after this commit.

inputContract.parentProducer: D12.12-H1 Python consumer arrays, already byte-exact to Node and independently replayed
forbiddenInputs: fixture ID in a per-pixel decision
directional class in a per-pixel decision
measured reconstruction error in a decision
a threshold selected after inspecting this derivation output

thresholdFamily.selectionRule: Select the largest candidate threshold, in the frozen descending order, that passes every safety, quality, primary coverage, per-owner retention, static, repeat and cross-language gate. If none passes, derive no candidate.
thresholdFamily.mathematicalCoupling: When measured risk underbound count is zero, accepted iff eligible and max(riskQ30)<=T, and T<=32768, every accepted RGB error is <=32768/2^30=3.0517578125e-5.
thresholdFamily.reconstruction: Reuse the immutable H1 reconstruction at newly accepted pixels; all newly rejected pixels must fall back byte-exactly to current RGBA.
thresholdFamily.globalPolicyScope: Thresholding applies to full-stencil and one-sided eligible pixels alike. It intentionally tests a global quality-safe risk policy, not a one-sided-only exception.

coverageGates.denominator: Every immutable H1 radius-2 current Material-owner cell. No support, risk, error or fixture-class reject may be removed.

directionalDiagnostics.decisionRole: report-only; never a selection gate because H1 proved TOP/BOTTOM/NEITHER fixtures did not generate their target domains
directionalDiagnostics.forbiddenClaim: A threshold candidate cannot repair the D12.12-H1 directional or neither-side verdict.

requiredFamilies: H1 parent byte and formal-tree mutation
spec, tool, runtime, process and operation-count mutation
eligible, risk, reconstruction and current-RGBA payload mutation
threshold insertion, deletion, reorder, relabel and hidden search
inclusive comparison, Q30 scale and quality-coupling mutation
accepted set, fallback, risk-underbound, maximum and RMSE mutation
coverage denominator and per-owner retention mutation
current RGB decision dependence and future-error leakage
cross-language, repeat, result, execution and receipt mutation
attacks.independence: The auditor may use Python standard library and NumPy but may not import either consumer, analyzer or runner. Every counted attack mutates an isolated in-memory semantic payload and must fail at least one named gate.

decision.derivedWhen: At least one frozen candidate threshold passes every hard and coverage gate, and the mechanically selected value is the largest passing candidate.
decision.promotionBoundary: A derived threshold is only a post-hoc candidate for a separately preregistered fresh holdout with repaired directional fixtures and a normalized-container determinism contract. It does not alter D12.12-H1 and does not enter the production compiler.

nonClaims: nonplanar, lit, transparent, deforming or production-pass safety
